evidence.title: 83 Sciences is hiring a Founding AI Engineer
evidence.rawVisibleText:
🙋‍♀️ We're hiring a Founding AI Engineer at 83 Sciences! If you can envision yourself in this role, please fill out this form: https://lnkd.in/gCTq6-Yw 

The role:
The Founding AI Engineer will help design insight and discovery extraction models and ship tools for scientists. You’ll own the architecture and build the ML stack alongside our Chief Science Officer and work directly with the founders.

What you'll do:
- Ship enterprise-ready products across our platform: data capture, structured experimental records, querying, and analysis tools
- Build our AI systems: multimodal pipelines (vision models for handwritten notebook pages and drawn structures, speech-to-text at the bench), agents that reason over a lab's full experimental history, and models that predict outcomes and propose optimized process conditions
- Work directly with research partners; watch scientists use what you built, then improve it
- Help shape model architecture, data pipelines, and technical direction as an early team member
- Build the data engine that turns messy experimental data (synthesis notes, PXRD, characterization) into training-grade datasets

What we're looking for:
- 1+ years of experience managing technical projects at startups and team members or big companies / research labs (e.g., FAIR Chemistry, Google DeepMind, Microsoft Research, OpenAI, Anthropic Lila Sciences, MIT/Stanford/Berkeley/CMU/UToronto AI-for-science groups, or similar)
- Deep in at least two of: geometric deep learning (E(3)/SE(3)-equivariant GNNs), generative models (diffusion, flow matching), ML interatomic potentials
- A track record of shipping enterprise-ready products to real users, end to end, with FDE / customer facing technical experience a plus
- Comfort across the stack: you can get a feature all the way out the door & bias toward speed and ownership in a small, fast-moving team

Logistics: NYC in-person (negotiable for the right person). US work authorization required.

Nice to have: model architecture/fine-tuning experience; background in chemistry, materials science, or scientific tooling; familiarity with scientific data (spectra, diffraction patterns, instrument output), A first-author or major-contributor paper in ML-for-science, geometric ML, molecular/crystal generation, scientific agents, interatomic potentials, synthesis planning, or active learning.

evidence.title: Alloovium launches its project-documentation platform
evidence.rawVisibleText:
Today, we launched Alloovium (YC S26) on Y Combinator.

On major projects, documents aren't a neat pile, they're a web. One change on site means five documents to amend, and nobody catches the missed one until an auditor, regulator, or client's lawyer does.

Alloovium (YC S26) is the unifying layer. It reads everything a project produces from the tools teams already use, and turns it into cited answers and the documentation that moves the job forward. Every answer cites its exact source sentence. A human signs off on anything AI-drafted.

We're already live on projects in Australia and with YC's backing, we're expanding into the US through our Innovation Partner Program.

Our ask: construction is structurally viral, so one head contractor exposes us to ~50 other contractors a year. If you know head contractors, GCs, or ENR Top 400 firms in the US/North America, a warm intro goes a long way.

Their agents understand each company from the very first task.

evidence.title: Context.dev launches file parsing to Markdown
evidence.rawVisibleText:
The amount of engineering time spent parsing files is honestly kind of ridiculous.

Every product eventually needs to deal with PDFs, Word documents, PowerPoints, spreadsheets, HTML, images, source code, CSVs... and every format comes with its own parser, quirks, and edge cases.

So we built Parse.

You send us the raw file bytes, and we return clean, token-optimized Markdown that's ready for LLMs or your application.

It supports:
• PDFs
• Microsoft Office documents (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
• Images (with OCR)
• HTML & XML
• CSV, JSON, YAML
• Source code
• Markdown, plain text, and dozens of other formats

OCR is built in for scanned documents and images, hyperlinks are preserved, PDF page ranges are supported, and the output is designed to be as compact and model-friendly as possible.

No more maintaining a collection of file parsers just to get text into your application.

Just send bytes, get Markdown.

If this is interesting to you, let's chat.

evidence.title: Context.dev introduces API-first website monitors
evidence.rawVisibleText:
Today we're introducing Monitors 🕵️‍♂️

Most website monitoring products are built for humans to click around in a dashboard.

We built Monitors for developers building agentic products.

If your application needs to create and manage monitors on behalf of thousands of customers, you can now do it entirely through an API.

A few things it's designed for:

• Create and manage 10,000+ monitors programmatically
• Multi-tenant SaaS applications
• Webhook-based notifications when websites change
• Infrastructure you can embed directly into your own product

The goal with Context.dev (YC S26) has always been to provide web infrastructure, not just another dashboard.

Someone integrated it the moment we shipped it, 6 hours before this announcement, to wake up agents in their products when something interesting happens on the part of the web they care about.

If you're building products that depend on websites staying up-to-date, we'd love to hear what you're building.
